136:    文档本身可能有错，且会过期。

71:  * glue can use the lwIP header only because it never includes NuttX net
72:  * headers.
73:  *
74:  * Reading the two ethertype bytes by hand also keeps the comparison in network
75:  * byte order, so no htons() and no <arpa/inet.h> are needed, and it does not
76:  * assume the payload is 2-byte aligned.  ETH_PAD_SIZE is 0 in this port, so the
77:  * 802.3 header is exactly dest[6] + src[6] + type[2].
78:  */
79: 
80: #define BK7258_ETH_HDR_LEN      14u
81: #define BK7258_ETH_SRC_OFFSET    6u
82: #define BK7258_ETH_TYPE_OFFSET  12u
83: #define BK7258_ETHTYPE_EAPOL    0x888eu
84: #endif

136: /* Armino's connector callback for an Ethernet frame. The vendor pbuf is
137:  * copied into the NuttX queue and released only after the copy completes.
138:  *
139:  * EAPOL is split off before that copy, see the block below.
140:  */
141: 
142: void ethernetif_input(int iface, struct pbuf *p, uint8_t dst_idx)
143: {
144:   struct bk7258_vpkt *vpkt;
145:   struct pbuf *q;
146:   uint8_t *dst;
147:   (void)iface;
148:   (void)dst_idx;
149: 
150:   if (p == NULL || p->tot_len == 0 || p->tot_len > BK7258_WIFI_FRAME_MAX)
151:     {
152:       if (p != NULL)
153:         {
154:           pbuf_free(p);
155:         }
156:       return;
157:     }
158: 
159: #if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
160:   /* Hand EAPOL to wpa_supplicant instead of to the NuttX stack.
161:    *
162:    * Transcribed from the vendor's own bridge, ethernetif_input() in
163:    * cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/port/wlanif.c:331 -- there the
164:    * EAPOL test is likewise the first thing done to a frame, ahead of the netif
165:    * lookup, with this comment: "EAPOL must reach wpa_supplicant even when lwip
166:    * netif is not registered yet".
167:    *
168:    * Why it has to be here: the 4-way handshake is carried in 802.3 frames with
169:    * ethertype 0x888E, and every 802.3 frame arrives through this one function
170:    * (rwnx_rx.c:728, the tail of rwm_upload_data(), which is registered as
171:    * g_rwnx_connector.data_outbound_func in rw_ieee80211.c).  Without this
172:    * split, M1 was copied into the NuttX RX queue, where the network stack has
173:    * no consumer for 0x888E and drops it: wpa_supplicant reached ASSOCIATED,
174:    * armed its 10 s auth timeout, never saw M1, and the AP disassociated us
175:    * with reason 15 (4WAY_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT) about four seconds later.  Board-
176:    * verified three times per run in the sta-hwioctlfix image.
177:    *
178:    * Management frames were never affected, which is why auth/assoc/beacon all
179:    * worked: those take the separate rwnx_rx_mgmt_any() path.
180:    *
181:    * This gap was known and recorded, not newly discovered:
182:    * glue/include/wpa_compat/sk_intf.h:20-22 states that "EAPOL/WAI (0x888e)
183:    * demux to the WPA entity is the network bridge's job (plan 11.4.2), not this
184:    * header's" -- the bridge is this function, and the work was never done.
185:    *
186:    * The self-echo filter is the vendor's too: our own transmitted EAPOL can be
187:    * looped back by the MAC, and feeding it to the supplicant would corrupt the
188:    * handshake state machine.  Frames whose source is our own address are
189:    * dropped rather than forwarded.
190:    *
191:    * Runtime-gated because ke_l2_packet_tx() lives in sk_intf.c, which is only
192:    * compiled under CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME (CMakeLists.txt:158); the
193:    * runtime-disabled CP image must not reference it.
194:    */
195: 
196:   if (p->len > BK7258_ETH_HDR_LEN)
197:     {
198:       FAR const uint8_t *eth = (FAR const uint8_t *)p->payload;
199:       uint16_t ethtype = ((uint16_t)eth[BK7258_ETH_TYPE_OFFSET] << 8) |
200:                           (uint16_t)eth[BK7258_ETH_TYPE_OFFSET + 1u];
201: 
202:       if (ethtype == BK7258_ETHTYPE_EAPOL)
203:         {
204:           struct ke_sk_params params;
205:           uint8_t own_mac[6];
206: 
207:           /* The vendor bridge compares the frame's source against the vif's
208:            * in-RAM MAC (wlanif.c: wifi_netif_vif_to_mac(vif)).  Our equivalent
209:            * is the vendor's own accessor: it resolves to bk_get_mac(), which
210:            * caches the address in RAM after one flash read at first use
211:            * (hal_port_mac.c:126-137) -- so this stays cheap on the RX path.
212:            * bk7258_wifi_board_get_mac() was rejected for exactly that reason:
213:            * it re-reads the flash partition on every call, here inside the
214:            * core thread during the 4-way window. */
215: 
216:           if (bk_wifi_sta_get_mac(own_mac) == BK_OK &&
217:               memcmp(own_mac, eth + BK7258_ETH_SRC_OFFSET,
218:                      sizeof(own_mac)) == 0)
219:             {
220:               pbuf_free(p);
221:               return;
222:             }
223: 
224:           /* buf/len describe the whole 802.3 frame, header included, exactly
225:            * as the vendor bridge passes it. */
226: 
227:           params.buf  = (unsigned char *)p->payload;
228:           params.len  = p->len;
229:           params.flag = iface;
230:           params.freq = 0;
231: 
232:           ke_l2_packet_tx(&params);
233:           pbuf_free(p);
234:           return;
235:         }
236:     }
237: #endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME */
238: 
239:   vpkt = bk7258_vpkt_alloc(p->tot_len, true);
240:   if (vpkt == NULL)
241:     {
242:       pbuf_free(p);
243:       return;
244:     }
245: 
246:   dst = vpkt->payload;
247:   for (q = p; q != NULL; q = q->next)
248:     {
249:       memcpy(dst, q->payload, q->len);
250:       dst += q->len;
251:     }
252:   bk7258_wifi_lower_rx_submit(&g_bk7258_wifi, vpkt);
253:   pbuf_free(p);
254: }

256: /****************************************************************************
257:  * Data plane
258:  *
259:  * transmit/receive stay disconnected until the vendor MAC TX/RX entry points
260:  * are wired. Returning -ENOSYS from transmit makes the upper half recycle the
261:  * NetPKT; returning NULL from receive signals "no packet available".
262:  ****************************************************************************/
263: 
264: static int bk7258_wifi_ifup(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower)
265: {
266:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv =
267:     (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
268: 
269:   /* Administrative up only.  Carrier is owned by the association events
270:    * (bk7258_wifi_sta_connected/disconnected) and must not be touched here: an
271:    * interface is legitimately brought up before associating, and clearing the
272:    * flag on ifup would desync this mirror from the IFF_RUNNING bit that
273:    * netdev_carrier_on/off actually own -- including the case where ifconfig up
274:    * follows a successful connect. */
275: 
276:   (void)priv;
277:   return OK;
278: }
279: 
280: static int bk7258_wifi_ifdown(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower)
281: {
282:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv =
283:     (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
284: 
285:   /* Administrative down only; carrier is owned by the association events for
286:    * the same reason as in ifup above.  Taking the interface down does not
287:    * disassociate, so the link -- and therefore the carrier -- outlives it. */
288: 
289:   (void)priv;
290:   return OK;
291: }
292: 
293: /* Hand a filled vendor pbuf to the vendor TX queue and release our reference.
294:  *
295:  * Split out so the netdev data path and the bring-up TX probe share the one
296:  * piece with non-obvious semantics: bmsg_tx_sender() takes its own reference
297:  * and drops it again if the queue push fails, so the reference from
298:  * pbuf_alloc() is ours to release on every path.  The two callers differ only
299:  * in where the bytes come from, which is why the allocation stays with them.
300:  */
301: 
302: static int bk7258_wifi_tx_pbuf(FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv,
303:                                struct pbuf *p)
304: {
305:   int ret = bmsg_tx_sender(p, priv->vif_idx);
306: 
307:   pbuf_free(p);
308: 
309:   if (ret != BK_OK)
310:     {
311:       /* The low-heap early return in bmsg_tx_sender() is the one case that is
312:        * not a transport failure, and the upper half retries on -ENOMEM. */
313: 
314:       return ret == BK_ERR_NO_MEM ? -ENOMEM : -EIO;
315:     }
316: 
317:   return OK;
318: }
319: 
320: static int bk7258_wifi_transmit(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower,
321:                                 FAR netpkt_t *pkt)
322: {
323:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
324:   struct pbuf *p;
325:   unsigned int len;
326:   int ret;
327: 
328:   len = netpkt_getdatalen(lower, pkt);
329:   if (len == 0 || len > BK7258_WIFI_FRAME_MAX)
330:     {
331:       return -EMSGSIZE;
332:     }
333: 
334:   p = pbuf_alloc(PBUF_RAW_TX, (u16_t)len, PBUF_RAM);
335:   if (p == NULL)
336:     {
337:       return -ENOMEM;
338:     }
339: 
340:   ret = netpkt_copyout(lower, p->payload, pkt, len, 0);
341:   if (ret < 0)
342:     {
343:       pbuf_free(p);
344:       return ret;
345:     }
346: 
347:   ret = bk7258_wifi_tx_pbuf(priv, p);
348:   if (ret < 0)
349:     {
350:       return ret;
351:     }
352: 
353:   netpkt_free(lower, pkt, NETPKT_TX);
354:   netdev_lower_txdone(lower);
355:   return OK;
356: }
357: 
358: static FAR netpkt_t *bk7258_wifi_receive(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower)
359: {
360:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
361:   FAR struct iob_s *iob;
362:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
363: 
364:   iob = priv->rx_head;
365:   if (iob != NULL)
366:     {
367:       priv->rx_head = iob->io_flink;
368:       if (priv->rx_head == NULL)
369:         {
370:           priv->rx_tail = NULL;
371:         }
372:       iob->io_flink = NULL;
373:     }
374: 
375:   leave_critical_section(flags);
376:   return iob;
377: }

379: static void bk7258_wifi_reclaim(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower)
380: {
381:   /* Genuinely nothing to reclaim, rather than a stub.
382:    *
383:    * netdev_upper_can_tx() (netdev_upperhalf.c:248-256) calls this when the TX
384:    * quota has run out, giving a driver the chance to walk its hardware
385:    * descriptors and release the netpkts it still owns.  This driver never owns
386:    * one past the transmit call: bk7258_wifi_transmit() copies the payload into a
387:    * vendor pbuf, hands that to bmsg_tx_sender(), and frees the netpkt before
388:    * returning, so quota is returned on the same call stack that consumed it.
389:    *
390:    * Kept in netdev_ops_s regardless.  Without it can_tx() has no recovery path
391:    * at all, and quota loss would then be permanently fatal instead of merely
392:    * costing one poll cycle. */
393: }

415: static int bk7258_wifi_essid(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower,
416:                              FAR struct iwreq *iwr, bool set)
417: {
418: #if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
419:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
420:   size_t len;
421: 
422:   /* Scan-SSID selection only.  This does NOT associate: the STA-only
423:    * bring-up contract forbids submitting credentials or associating before
424:    * scan discovers an AP, so SIOCSIWESSID here records which SSID the next
425:    * scan should probe for and nothing else.
426:    *
427:    * NuttX has no struct iw_scan_req, so a directed scan is expressed the
428:    * standard WEXT way: SIOCSIWESSID followed by SIOCSIWSCAN. */
429: 
430:   if (iwr == NULL)
431:     {
432:       return -EINVAL;
433:     }
434: 
435:   if (!set)
436:     {
437:       len = priv->scan_ssid_len;
438:       if (iwr->u.essid.pointer == NULL || iwr->u.essid.length < len)
439:         {
440:           return -EINVAL;
441:         }
442: 
443:       memcpy(iwr->u.essid.pointer, priv->scan_ssid, len);
444:       iwr->u.essid.length = (uint16_t)len;
445:       iwr->u.essid.flags = len > 0u ? 1u : 0u;
446:       return OK;
447:     }
448: 
449:   /* flags == 0 means "any SSID" -> clear back to a broadcast scan. */
450: 
451:   if (iwr->u.essid.flags == 0u || iwr->u.essid.pointer == NULL)
452:     {
453:       priv->scan_ssid_len = 0u;
454:       priv->scan_ssid[0] = '\0';
455:       return OK;
456:     }
457: 
458:   len = iwr->u.essid.length;
459: 
460:   /* Some WEXT callers include the terminator in length; drop it. */
461: 
462:   if (len > 0u && ((FAR const char *)iwr->u.essid.pointer)[len - 1u] == '\0')
463:     {
464:       len--;
465:     }
466: 
467:   if (len > BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_SSID_LEN)
468:     {
469:       return -EINVAL;
470:     }
471: 
472:   memcpy(priv->scan_ssid, iwr->u.essid.pointer, len);
473:   priv->scan_ssid[len] = '\0';
474:   priv->scan_ssid_len = (uint8_t)len;
475:   return OK;
476: #else
477:   return -ENOSYS;
478: #endif
479: }

511: static int bk7258_wifi_scan(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower,
512:                             FAR struct iwreq *iwr, bool set)
513: {
514: #if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
515:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *)lower;
516:   size_t required = 0;
517:   size_t ssid_len;
518:   uint8_t index;
519:   int ret;
520: 
521:   if (!priv->scan_lock_ready)
522:     {
523:       return -ENODEV;
524:     }
525: 
526:   if (set)
527:     {
528:       nxmutex_lock(&priv->scan_lock);
529:       if (priv->scan_in_progress)
530:         {
531:           nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
532:           return -EBUSY;
533:         }
534: 
535:       /* bk_wifi_scan_start() records this exact caller token in its scan
536:        * request, then returns it in wifi_event_scan_done_t.scan_id. */
537: 
538:       priv->scan_id = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)rtos_get_current_thread();
539:       priv->scan_in_progress = true;
540:       priv->scan_complete = false;
541:       priv->scan_status = -EAGAIN;
542:       priv->scan_count = 0;
543:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
544: 
545:       bk7258_scan_diag_begin();
546: 
547:       /* Directed vs broadcast scan.  The authority reference run was a
548:        * DIRECTED scan (`scanu_start_req ... ssid_len=3`) while ours has always
549:        * been broadcast (`ssid_len=0`); aligning that removes one difference
550:        * from the comparison.  Config built exactly like the vendor's own
551:        * callers do (zeroed struct, ssid copied, everything else left 0). */
552: 
553:       if (priv->scan_ssid_len > 0u)
554:         {
555:           wifi_scan_config_t cfg;
556: 
557:           memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
558:           memcpy(cfg.ssid, priv->scan_ssid, priv->scan_ssid_len);
559:           syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] scan: directed len=%u\n",
560:                  (unsigned)priv->scan_ssid_len);
561:           ret = bk_wifi_scan_start(&cfg);
562:         }
563:       else
564:         {
565:           ret = bk_wifi_scan_start(NULL);
566:         }
567: 
568:       if (ret != BK_OK)
569:         {
570:           bk7258_scan_diag_record(BK7258_SCAN_DIAG_START_REJECTED);
571:           nxmutex_lock(&priv->scan_lock);
572:           priv->scan_in_progress = false;
573:           priv->scan_complete = true;
574:           priv->scan_status = ret == BK_ERR_BUSY ? -EBUSY : -EIO;
575:           nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
576:           return priv->scan_status;
577:         }
578: 
579:       bk7258_scan_diag_record(BK7258_SCAN_DIAG_START_ACCEPTED);
580: 
581:       return OK;
582:     }
583: 
584:   if (iwr == NULL)
585:     {
586:       return -EINVAL;
587:     }
588: 
589:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->scan_lock);
590:   if (priv->scan_in_progress)
591:     {
592:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
593:       return -EAGAIN;
594:     }
595: 
596:   if (!priv->scan_complete)
597:     {
598:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
599:       return -EINVAL;
600:     }
601: 
602:   if (priv->scan_status < 0)
603:     {
604:       ret = priv->scan_status;
605:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
606:       return ret;
607:     }
608: 
609:   /* Calculate the full WEXT event stream before writing user storage. This
610:    * avoids returning partial results or exposing an incomplete AP record. */
611: 
612:   for (index = 0; index < priv->scan_count; index++)
613:     {
614:       ssid_len = strnlen(priv->scan_aps[index].ssid,
615:                          BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_SSID_LEN);
616:       required += IW_EV_LEN(ap_addr) + IW_EV_LEN(qual) + IW_EV_LEN(freq) +
617:                   IW_EV_LEN(data) + IW_EV_LEN(essid) +
618:                   ((ssid_len + 3u) & ~3u);
619:     }
620: 
621:   if (required > UINT16_MAX || iwr->u.data.pointer == NULL ||
622:       required > iwr->u.data.length)
623:     {
624:       iwr->u.data.length = required > UINT16_MAX ? UINT16_MAX : required;
625:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
626:       return -E2BIG;
627:     }
628: 
629:   {
630:     FAR uint8_t *cursor = iwr->u.data.pointer;
631: 
632:     for (index = 0; index < priv->scan_count; index++)
633:       {
634:         FAR struct iw_event *iwe = (FAR struct iw_event *)cursor;
635:         FAR struct bk7258_wifi_scan_ap_s *ap = &priv->scan_aps[index];
636:         iwe->cmd = SIOCGIWAP;
637:         iwe->u.ap_addr.sa_family = ARPHRD_ETHER;
638:         memcpy(iwe->u.ap_addr.sa_data, ap->bssid, sizeof(ap->bssid));
639:         iwe->len = IW_EV_LEN(ap_addr);
640:         cursor += iwe->len;
641: 
642:         ssid_len = strnlen(ap->ssid, BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_SSID_LEN);
643:         iwe = (FAR struct iw_event *)cursor;
644:         iwe->cmd = SIOCGIWESSID;
645:         iwe->u.essid.flags = 0;
646:         iwe->u.essid.length = ssid_len;
647:         iwe->u.essid.pointer = (FAR void *)sizeof(iwe->u.essid);
648:         memcpy(&iwe->u.essid + 1, ap->ssid, ssid_len);
649:         iwe->len = IW_EV_LEN(essid) + ((ssid_len + 3u) & ~3u);
650:         cursor += iwe->len;
651: 
652:         iwe = (FAR struct iw_event *)cursor;
653:         iwe->cmd = IWEVQUAL;
654:         iwe->u.qual.qual = 0;
655:         iwe->u.qual.level = (uint8_t)ap->rssi;
656:         iwe->u.qual.noise = 0;
657:         iwe->u.qual.updated = IW_QUAL_LEVEL_UPDATED | IW_QUAL_DBM |
658:                               IW_QUAL_QUAL_INVALID | IW_QUAL_NOISE_INVALID;
659:         iwe->len = IW_EV_LEN(qual);
660:         cursor += iwe->len;
661: 
662:         iwe = (FAR struct iw_event *)cursor;
663:         iwe->cmd = SIOCGIWFREQ;
664:         /* WEXT represents values 0..1000 as a channel number. This avoids
665:          * inventing a frequency conversion for a future/non-2.4GHz result. */
666:         iwe->u.freq.e = 0;
667:         iwe->u.freq.m = ap->channel;
668:         iwe->len = IW_EV_LEN(freq);
669:         cursor += iwe->len;
670: 
671:         iwe = (FAR struct iw_event *)cursor;
672:         iwe->cmd = SIOCGIWENCODE;
673:         iwe->u.data.flags = ap->security == WIFI_SECURITY_NONE ?
674:                             IW_ENCODE_DISABLED :
675:                             IW_ENCODE_ENABLED | IW_ENCODE_NOKEY;
676:         iwe->u.data.length = 0;
677:         iwe->u.data.pointer = NULL;
678:         iwe->len = IW_EV_LEN(data);
679:         cursor += iwe->len;
680:       }
681: 
682:     iwr->u.data.length = cursor - (FAR uint8_t *)iwr->u.data.pointer;
683:   }
684: 
685:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
686:   return OK;
687: #else
688:   (void)lower;
689:   (void)iwr;
690:   (void)set;
691:   return -ENOSYS;
692: #endif
693: }

732: int bk7258_wifi_lower_init(struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv)
733: {
734:   memset(priv, 0, sizeof(*priv));
735: 
736:   if (nxmutex_init(&priv->scan_lock) < 0)
737:     {
738:       return -ENOMEM;
739:     }
740: 
741:   priv->scan_lock_ready = true;
742: 
743: #if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
744:   {
745:     bk_err_t ret = bk_event_register_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_SCAN_DONE,
746:                                         bk7258_wifi_scan_done, priv);
747: 
748:     if (ret != BK_OK && ret != BK_ERR_EVENT_CB_EXIST)
749:       {
750:         nxmutex_destroy(&priv->scan_lock);
751:         priv->scan_lock_ready = false;
752:         return -EIO;
753:       }
754: 
755:     priv->scan_callback_registered = true;
756: 
757:     /* Association and disconnection drive the carrier flag; see the comment
758:      * above bk7258_wifi_sta_connected() for why carrier is dynamic here while
759:      * the authority keeps NETIF_FLAG_LINK_UP constant.
760:      *
761:      * Treated as fatal for the same reason the scan callback above is: if the
762:      * event module cannot take a callback, nothing about this driver works, and
763:      * a netdev whose carrier can never rise would accept an ifconfig and then
764:      * silently refuse to carry traffic. */
765: 
766:     ret = bk_event_register_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_STA_CONNECTED,
767:                                bk7258_wifi_sta_connected, priv);
768:     if (ret == BK_OK || ret == BK_ERR_EVENT_CB_EXIST)
769:       {
770:         ret = bk_event_register_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_STA_DISCONNECTED,
771:                                    bk7258_wifi_sta_disconnected, priv);
772:         if (ret != BK_OK && ret != BK_ERR_EVENT_CB_EXIST)
773:           {
774:             (void)bk_event_unregister_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI,
775:                                          EVENT_WIFI_STA_CONNECTED,
776:                                          bk7258_wifi_sta_connected);
777:           }
778:       }
779: 
780:     if (ret != BK_OK && ret != BK_ERR_EVENT_CB_EXIST)
781:       {
782:         (void)bk_event_unregister_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_SCAN_DONE,
783:                                      bk7258_wifi_scan_done);
784:         priv->scan_callback_registered = false;
785:         nxmutex_destroy(&priv->scan_lock);
786:         priv->scan_lock_ready = false;
787:         return -EIO;
788:       }
789: 
790:     priv->sta_event_registered = true;
791:   }
792: #endif
793: 
794:   return 0;
795: }

834:       nxmutex_destroy(&priv->scan_lock);
835:       priv->scan_lock_ready = false;
836:     }
837: 
838:   return 0;
839: }

841: #if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
842: static bk_err_t bk7258_wifi_scan_done(void *arg, event_module_t module,
843:                                       int event_id, void *event_data)
844: {
845:   FAR struct bk7258_wifi_s *priv = arg;
846:   FAR wifi_event_scan_done_t *done = event_data;
847:   wifi_scan_result_t result = {0};
848:   int ret;
849:   int ap_num;
850:   int index;
851:   struct bk7258_scan_diag_s diag;
852: 
853:   if (priv == NULL || module != EVENT_MOD_WIFI ||
854:       event_id != EVENT_WIFI_SCAN_DONE || done == NULL ||
855:       !priv->scan_lock_ready)
856:     {
857:       return BK_OK;
858:     }
859: 
860:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->scan_lock);
861:   if (!priv->scan_in_progress || done->scan_id != priv->scan_id)
862:     {
863:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
864:       return BK_OK;
865:     }
866:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
867: 
868:   bk7258_scan_diag_record(BK7258_SCAN_DIAG_COMPLETION_CALLBACK);
869: 
870:   /* The SDK allocates result.aps. Copy the bounded data below, then release
871:    * it unconditionally before this synchronous event callback returns. */
872: 
873:   ret = bk_wifi_scan_get_result(&result);
874:   if (ret != BK_OK)
875:     {
876:       bk7258_scan_diag_record(BK7258_SCAN_DIAG_RESULT_FETCH_FAIL);
877:     }
878: 
879:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->scan_lock);
880:   if (priv->scan_in_progress && done->scan_id == priv->scan_id)
881:     {
882:       priv->scan_count = 0;
883:       priv->scan_status = ret == BK_OK ? OK : -EIO;
884: 
885:       if (ret == BK_OK && result.ap_num > 0 && result.aps != NULL)
886:         {
887:           ap_num = result.ap_num;
888:           if (ap_num > BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS)
889:             {
890:               ap_num = BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS;
891:             }
892: 
893:           for (index = 0; index < ap_num; index++)
894:             {
895:               FAR struct bk7258_wifi_scan_ap_s *dst = &priv->scan_aps[index];
896:               FAR wifi_scan_ap_info_t *src = &result.aps[index];
897: 
898:               memset(dst, 0, sizeof(*dst));
899:               memcpy(dst->ssid, src->ssid, BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_SSID_LEN);
900:               dst->ssid[BK7258_WIFI_SCAN_SSID_LEN] = '\0';
901:               memcpy(dst->bssid, src->bssid, sizeof(dst->bssid));
902:               dst->rssi = src->rssi;
903:               dst->channel = src->channel;
904:               dst->security = (uint32_t)src->security;
905:             }
906: 
907:           priv->scan_count = ap_num;
908:         }
909: 
910:       priv->scan_in_progress = false;
911:       priv->scan_complete = true;
912:     }
913:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->scan_lock);
914: 
915:   bk7258_scan_diag_result_exported(ret == BK_OK && result.ap_num > 0 ?
916:                                   (uint32_t)result.ap_num : 0);
917:   bk7258_scan_diag_snapshot(&diag);
918:   {
919:     /* EVERY MODEM-DOMAIN REGISTER READ IN THIS CALLBACK WAS REMOVED
920:      * (2026-09-08), for the same reason the parity banner's snapshot was:
921:      * NXMAC (0x49100000/0x49108000), the modem clock (0x49000000) and CRM
922:      * (0x49850000) all sit behind the MAC's clock gate, and with
923:      * CONFIG_PM_V2 && CONFIG_STA_PS compiled in the MAC is put into doze by
924:      * rwnxl_sleep() at the tail of rwnx_intf_init() (rw_task.c:1245) and is
925:      * re-woken only inside the core thread, by mac_wakeup_and_pwr_update()
926:      * (rw_task.c:821), for the duration of the work it dequeued.  A read of
927:      * a gated register stalls the AHB load forever: the CPU never retires
928:      * the instruction, so nothing faults (CONFIG_DEBUG_BUSFAULT reports bus
929:      * ERRORS, not stalls) and no other thread runs to print a clue.  The
930:      * banner version of this hang looked exactly like a silent console with
931:      * no nsh prompt and zero bytes of UART response.
932:      *
933:      * This callback runs on the event/app thread, NOT on the core thread, so
934:      * it has no wake guarantee at all -- the MAC may re-enter doze between
935:      * the scan completing and this callback being dispatched.  The removed
936:      * reads were written when rwnxl_sleep() was not compiled and the MAC
937:      * stayed awake for the whole session, which is why they used to work.
938:      *
939:      * The authority's own scan-done path reads no MAC register, so deleting
940:      * these converges on it rather than diverging.
941:      *
942:      * If MAC state has to be sampled again, sample it from a context that
943:      * owns a wake: inside the core thread while it is handling a BMSG (i.e.
944:      * after mac_wakeup_and_pwr_update() for that message), or from a
945:      * library callback that already runs with the MAC active.  Do NOT guard
946:      * such a read by reading a MAC register first -- that probe is itself
947:      * the stall.  The only safe status sources are the always-on SYS domain
948:      * (0x44010000, e.g. BK7258_SYS_POWER_WAKEUP below), libwifi's own RAM
949:      * (ke_state_get(), the ps_env flags) and AON PMU.
950:      *
951:      * Kept below: reads that cannot stall.  chan_env/txl_cntrl_env are SRAM
952:      * symbols resolved at link time; the OFDM/wakeup word is SYS-domain;
953:      * the ISR counters, the MM task state and the sd1..sd5 counters are all
954:      * plain memory. */
955:     extern uint8_t chan_env[];
956:     extern uint8_t txl_cntrl_env[];
957: 
958:     /* Console is 80 columns and overwrites past ~79 chars, so every
959:      * diagnostic keeps its payload under ~65 chars after the tag.  Three
960:      * consecutive boards lost fields to this (vcorehsel twice, the whole
961:      * MMSTART post line once), which is why these are split. */
962: 
963:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] d2b chan=%08lx txhalt=%04x\n",
964:            (unsigned long)*(volatile uint32_t *)(chan_env + 0x28),
965:            (unsigned int)*(volatile uint16_t *)(txl_cntrl_env + 0x16e));
966: 
967:     /* SYS domain only (0x44010000 is never gated): the OFDM power-down vote
968:      * the library reads back through crm_mdm_reset, and the raw wakeup
969:      * word it lives in.  The `crm14=` field that used to close this line
970:      * read 0x49850014 and went with the rest. */
971: 
972:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] d3a ofdm=%lu pwak=%08lx\n",
973:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_pwd_ofdm_get_override(),
974:            (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_SYS_POWER_WAKEUP));
975:   }
976:   {
977:     extern volatile uint32_t bk7258_wifi_isr_count[64];
978:     extern int ke_state_get(uint8_t task_id);
979: 
980:     uint32_t state = (unsigned)ke_state_get(0);  /* TASK_MM = 0 */
981: 
982:     /* THREE PROBES DELETED HERE (2026-09-01) -- all three dereferenced
983:      * hard-coded closed-library RAM addresses that have since DRIFTED:
984:      *
985:      *   cm      0x280700c0 -> now lands in socket_entity+4 (a 12-byte symbol)
986:      *   in_doze 0x2807bdb1 -> now lands in scanu_env+733
987:      *   lowpll  0x2807bdb8 -> now lands in scanu_env+740
988:      *
989:      * Proof of drift, measured in THIS session: chan_env / txl_cntrl_env /
990:      * rwnx_env / ke_env each moved by exactly +0x28 between two builds,
991:      * because adding scan_ssid[33]+scan_ssid_len to struct bk7258_wifi_s
992:      * pushed every following BSS symbol along.  Any literal address into
993:      * library RAM is invalidated by an unrelated struct change.
994:      *
995:      * Consequence that must be carried forward: the repeated
996:      * "in_doze=0 lowpll=0, therefore the MAC is not sleeping" conclusion is
997:      * WITHDRAWN for our side -- those bytes were never the doze status.  The
998:      * authority board's own in_doze probe is unaffected (its build, its
999:      * addresses).
1000:      *
1001:      * Rule: reach library state through a linkable global (extern) or a
1002:      * function call, never through a literal.  chan_env/txl_cntrl_env below
1003:      * are `extern` and therefore resolved at link time; ke_state_get is a
1004:      * call.  Those stay. */
1005: 
1006:     /* Per-source interrupt counts.  The library registers seven handlers via
1007:      * _bk_int_isr_register (board log: sources 36,35,34,33,31,30,29) and the
1008:      * counters have been collected all along in hw_driver_shim.c -- only
1009:      * index 36 was ever printed.  For the stalled directed scan the decisive
1010:      * one is 34 (MAC TX trigger): the probe frame reaches txl_frame_push yet
1011:      * `frame released without call cb` says its confirm never ran, so either
1012:      * the completion interrupt never arrives (count 0 -> enable/routing, or
1013:      * the MAC never raised it) or it arrives and the dispatch chain drops it
1014:      * (count > 0 -> the HISR/workqueue semantics).
1015:      * Source map (Armino sys_struct.h:463-465 + high-bank bits 0-4):
1016:      *   29 modem_mpb  30 modem_riu  31 mac_txrx_timer
1017:      *   32 txrx_misc  33 rx_trigger 34 tx_trigger  35 prot  36 gen */
1018: 
1019:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] isr 29=%lu 30=%lu 31=%lu 32=%lu\n",
1020:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[29],
1021:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[30],
1022:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[31],
1023:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[32]);
1024:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] isr 33=%lu 34=%lu 35=%lu 36=%lu\n",
1025:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[33],
1026:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[34],
1027:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[35],
1028:            (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[36]);
1029:     syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] mmstate=%lu\n", (unsigned long)state);
1030:     /* WPROBE3 REMOVED (2026-09-01).  It hard-coded 0x2806fb90 as "the hal env
1031:      * pointer" and dereferenced +0xe4/e8/ec/f8 as setfreq inputs.  nm proves
1032:      * that word holds the closed library's saved FUNCS-TABLE pointer
1033:      * (0x2806f810 = g_wifi_os_funcs), so all four "inputs" resolved +0 to our
1034:      * own slot functions (hp_uap_ip_start, hp_uap_ip_down,
1035:      * hp_net_wlan_add_netif, bk7258_wifi_set_sta_status_cb).  Every reading it
1036:      * produced was garbage.
1037:      *
1038:      * The wider lesson (user directive): hard-referencing closed-library
1039:      * internal RAM from outside is not how this port gets fixed.  Eight such
1040:      * probe-driven candidates were falsified this session, while all six real
1041:      * defects came from diffing OUR sources against Armino's sources.
1042:      * Hardware registers stay fair game -- their semantics are recoverable
1043:      * from Armino's own accessor functions -- but library-internal addresses
1044:      * are not.  Remaining offenders of this kind, kept only because they at
1045:      * least report what they claim: the 0x2807bdb1/0x2807bdb8 doze bytes
1046:      * above and the chan_env/txl_cntrl_env externs in scan diag2. */
1047:     /* The "M1: 49108050" line was REMOVED with the rest of the modem-domain
1048:      * reads (2026-09-08).  0x49108050 is in the MAC interrupt block and is
1049:      * gated with the MAC, so reading it here stalls exactly like the others.
1050:      * What it reported -- that hal_machw_init() reached its interrupt-enable
1051:      * step -- is already implied by the scan producing results at all, and
1052:      * by the isr counters printed above (a nonzero count for source 33/34/36
1053:      * cannot happen unless the MAC's interrupt enable was programmed). */
1054:   }
1055:   /* The [NXWIN] register-window dump was REMOVED (2026-09-08): 44 words of
1056:    * getreg32(0x49100000 + n) is the single largest concentration of gated
1057:    * NXMAC reads in the tree, and the first iteration is enough to wedge the
1058:    * CPU on a doze'd MAC.
1059:    *
1060:    * It was a parity tool, not a runtime diagnostic -- its whole purpose was
1061:    * to be diffed against the same dump taken on the authority board.  If
1062:    * that comparison is needed again, take it from a context that holds a
1063:    * wake (see the note at the head of this callback), or better, take it on
1064:    * both boards with STA_PS off in a throwaway image whose only job is the
1065:    * dump; do not carry it in the normal scan path.
1066:    */
1067:   /* The `d3f` probe that used to sit here is DELETED (2026-09-01).
1068:    *
1069:    * It sampled 0x49100010 twice across a 200 us delay and printed it as
1070:    * `tick=`, on the belief that the register was a free-running ke_timer /
1071:    * mm_timer counter.  It is not: 0x49100010 / 0x14 are the NXMAC MAC-ADDRESS
1072:    * registers (authority accessors nxmac_mac_addr_low_get / _hi_get read
1073:    * [base+0x10] / [base+0x14]), and the board proves it -- once bk_get_mac was
1074:    * fixed the pair went from 0/0 to 468c47c8 / 00001502, i.e. exactly the
1075:    * c8:47:8c:46:02:15 read out of flash, matching the authority byte for byte.
1076:    * So every earlier "the tick counter is dead" reading was really "the MAC
1077:    * address register is zero", and the 200 us delay measured nothing.
1078:    *
1079:    * NXWIN row 0x10 already prints both words, so nothing is lost by removing
1080:    * this.  0x491000ac was printed alongside it as `ac=` on an equally
1081:    * unverified guess (nxmac_lp_clk_32786_hz_setf) and is dropped with it. */
1082: 
1083:   /* MM_RESET/MM_START hardware latches, re-reported from this quiet context.
1084:    * Printing at the sample sites raced with other threads' console output: on
1085:    * sta-mmstate-20260901 the `post` line vanished and the `pre` line was cut
1086:    * in half, losing the only measurement that image existed to take.
1087:    *
1088:    * DO NOT read ke=0 / r38=0 at the post-start column as "mm_active() never
1089:    * ran".  A three-way table saying that was written here once and is wrong:
1090:    * mm_start_req_handler sends the CFM *before* it calls mm_active() and
1091:    * ke_state_set(), then parks the MAC via hal_machw_idle_req().  So the
1092:    * instant rw_msg_send() returns is either ahead of mm_active() or already
1093:    * past the park, and ke=0 / r38=0 there is the expected success path.
1094:    * Board evidence (sta-arminoalign-20260902): all four columns read ke=0,
1095:    * r38=0, ret=0, while the end-of-scan probe reports mmstate=MM_ACTIVE(1)
1096:    * and r38=0x33 -- MM did start.  These four columns therefore say nothing
1097:    * about MM bring-up; they are only useful for registers that are expected
1098:    * to be stable across the whole handshake.
1099:    * States: 0=MM_IDLE 1=MM_ACTIVE 2=GOING_TO_IDLE 3=HOST_BYPASSED
1100:    *         4=MM_NO_IDLE (lmac_msg.h:885-899).  ke=-1 marks a site that has
1101:    *         no ke_state to report (the two reset points).

1652: int bk7258_wifi_sta_connect(FAR const char *ssid, FAR const char *psk)
1653: {

1655:   size_t ssid_len;
1656:   size_t psk_len;

1661:       return -EINVAL;
1662:     }
1663:

1701:              (unsigned)(sizeof(config.password) - 1u));

1706:    * load-bearing rather than incidental:

1717:   memcpy(config.ssid, ssid, ssid_len);
1718:   memcpy(config.password, psk, psk_len);

1720:   /* SSID and lengths only.  The passphrase itself is never logged, here or
1721:    * in the status path. */

1723:   if (psk_len == 0u)
1724:     {
1725:       syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] connect: ssid=\"%s\" (%u), open\n",

1727:     }
1728:   else
1729:     {
1730:       syslog(LOG_INFO, "[BK7258-WIFI] connect: ssid=\"%s\" (%u), psk %u chars\n",

1732:     }

1734:   /* set_config before start, as in the original.  set_config is also what

1738:    * set_config disconnects first and re-connects on its own
1739:    * (wifi_v2.c:2983-3010). */

1741:   ret = bk_wifi_sta_set_config(&config);
1742:   if (ret != BK_OK)
1743:     {
1744:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "[BK7258-WIFI] connect: set_config failed=%d\n",
1745:              (int)ret);
1746:       return -EIO;
1747:     }
1748: 
1749:   ret = bk_wifi_sta_start();
1750:   if (ret != BK_OK)
1751:     {

1794:       *reason = (int)info.reason_code;

1. **app 路径** = `app/bk7258_wifi_runtime/bk7258_wifi_runtime_main.c` 的 `connect` 子命令 → 直接调 `bk7258_wifi_sta_connect()` → 底层 `bk_wifi_sta_set_config()` + `bk_wifi_sta_start()`。这就是你说的"用的 app"。

1: # Branch topology, PR packaging, and the dead-code audit method
2: 
3: Six entries. Read before choosing a merge target, before restructuring commits, before deleting any `chips/bk7258` source, and before citing a firmware hash as evidence.
4: 
5: ## 1. Which ref is upstream (a wrong answer wastes a whole analysis)
6: 
7: - `openvela/dev-ai-contest-2026` is the REAL upstream and the PR base. `openvela` = `https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian`.
8: - `origin/dev-ai-contest-2026` is a STALE mirror inside the personal fork (`git@github.com:C-Luv9615/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian.git`), 27 commits behind the real upstream. Choosing it as a PR base silently ruins the PR.
9: - Local `dev` is a SIDE BRANCH, not an integration point: 11 behind the real upstream, 1 ahead (`7a48959` acp-bridge, which exists on no remote). `git merge-base --is-ancestor openvela/dev-ai-contest-2026 dev` → NO.
10: - User correction, verbatim: "不应该看dev 而是应该看openvela 的dev-ai-contest-2026". Measure divergence against the real upstream only.
11: - Worktree directory names do NOT match branch names. `.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild` held branch `wip-post-2a58eac`, while a DIFFERENT branch `feature/bk7258-wifi-rebuild` exists and is not its ancestor. Always confirm with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.
12: 
13: ## 2. Restructuring a long commit series without risking content loss
14: 
15: Method used to fold 55 commits into 21 (`pr/bk7258-wifi-network-bringup`, script kept at `/tmp/restructure-wifi.sh`): for each group, `git read-tree -u --reset <group-tail>` then commit. Each new commit's tree equals the original tail commit's tree BY CONSTRUCTION, so no hunk can be lost and no conflict can arise. Do NOT use `git rebase -i` for this.
16: 
17: Two constraints that make it safe:
18: 
19: - Only cut at boundaries of the ORIGINAL topological order. Grouping by theme across non-adjacent commits requires real cherry-picks and reintroduces conflict risk. A first attempt grouped by theme and had to be abandoned for this reason (55 → 21 with contiguous cuts, not 14 with themed cuts).
20: - The final group sets the tree to the original HEAD, which makes `git diff <original-HEAD> <new-HEAD>` empty by construction. Verify it anyway — that empty diff is the acceptance criterion for the whole operation.
21: 
22: Probe pairs that were added and later removed become net-zero automatically when both fall inside one group and neither is cherry-picked: `git diff <probe-add>^ <probe-remove>` empty proves it.
23: 
24: `git checkout -B <branch> <remote-ref>` inherits that REMOTE as upstream — pass `--no-track` when the new branch must push to a different remote.
25: 
26: ## 3. Reachability is the only valid dead-code test in this tree
27: 
28: `chips/bk7258` compiles vendor code by TEXT-INCLUDING it into a thin team-owned wrapper TU, so an authority `.c` never appears in any build file and grepping build lists alone reports live files as dead. The correct pass (script kept at `/tmp/reach.py`):
29: 
30: 1. Take roots from BOTH build systems: `chips/bk7258/{CMakeLists.txt,Make.defs}` and `chips/bk7258/wifi/{CMakeLists.txt,Make.defs}` plus `chips/bk7258/audio/CMakeLists.txt`. Strip `#` comments first — several dead files are named only in explanatory comments.
31: 2. Follow `#include "*.c"` and `#include "*.inc"` chains transitively from those roots.
32: 3. Anything unreached is a TU nothing can compile.
33: 
34: Result at 2026-09-16: 551 tracked `.c`/`.inc`, 171 roots, 213 reachable, 338 unreachable (322705 lines). Neither CMakeLists globs, so an explicit list is the only way in.
35: 
36: Two independent confirmations worth running on a candidate before deleting:
37: 
38: - No `.o` for it in the build output, against a known-live file as control.
39: - SYMBOL COLLISION, the strongest one: if the candidate defines a symbol that a COMPILED file also defines, it can never have been in the build (the link would fail on duplicates). This is what settled `rwnx_td_nuttx_adapter.c` (`rwnx_td_init`, `rwnx_get_td_info` already from the compiled `vendor_sources/rwnx_td.c` wrapper) and `glue/bk7258_saradc.c` (`bk_adc_*` already from the compiled `saradc/middleware/driver/saradc/adc_driver.c`).
40: 
41: Scope caveat: a repo-wide grep is needed, not a `chips/bk7258`-only one. `chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_spi.h` looked orphaned until `board/bk7258-devkit/src/bk7258_spi_hw.c:58` turned up.
42: 
43: ## 4. Header shadowing — `hal_port/vnd_cal.h` must NOT be deleted
44: 
45: `-I.../wifi/hal_port` precedes `-I.../third_party/beken_armino/board/bk7258/vnd_cal/include` on the command line, so the COMPILED `third_party/.../vnd_cal/vnd_cal.c`'s own `#include "vnd_cal.h"` resolves to OUR `hal_port/vnd_cal.h`, not to its sibling. The two headers differ (ours pulls `<common/bk_include.h>`; the vendored one pulls `bk_arm_arch.h` + `bk_misc.h`). Deleting the apparently-orphaned header silently switches that TU's header. Confirmed with `ninja -t deps`. Documented in the file's own top comment as of `f4af033`. Generalise: in this tree a header with no in-directory includer may still be load-bearing through `-I` ordering.
46: 
47: ## 5. A firmware sha256 is NOT portable evidence
48: 
49: NuttX bakes `__DATE__` into `nuttx/libs/libc/misc/lib_utsname.c`, so a clean build elsewhere always produces a different `all-app.bin` hash. Locally the hash DOES reproduce across days because `CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache` and ccache's `time_macros` sloppiness keeps the frozen date string in the cached object. Consequences:
50: 
51: - Never put a firmware sha256 in a PR description as something a reviewer can verify. Cite reproduction steps and committed log files instead.
52: - `--fresh` genuinely `rm -rf`s the build dir (`full_flow.sh:200-202`); a 6-second "build completed successfully" with all 2309 objects freshly dated is a full ccache hit, not a skipped build. That full hit is STRONGER evidence than hash equality: it means every TU's preprocessed input is byte-identical.
53: - The identical-hash-after-deletion test is the cleanest proof a deleted file was never compiled. Used for both cleanup rounds (`72ca6e3` 914 lines, `f4af033` 1201 lines) — 2115 lines removed, firmware `b1bc333e…` unchanged.
54: - An ELF mtime newer than its embedded `__DATE__` string is normal under ccache (relink without recompiling the version object), not evidence of a dirty build.
55: 
56: `vendor/beken/chips/bk7258` is a SYMLINK to the active worktree's `chips/bk7258`, which is why build artifacts carry `vendor/beken/...` paths. Verify with `readlink -f` before concluding a build read a different tree.
57: 
58: ## 6. What may not be deleted, and the two kinds of uncompiled authority file
59: 
60: `AGENTS.md:19-24` calls the vendor source "the local Armino authority tree", explicitly allows module-scoped imports into `chips/bk7258/`, requires retaining "the authority module structure and provenance", and forbids placing imported authority sources under `third_party/`. That wording is where the `authority/` directory name comes from.
61: 
62: Uncompiled but KEPT: 326 files under `wifi/third_party/beken_armino/` (319272 lines, mostly wpa_supplicant `src/ap/*`, `src/p2p/*` and alternate TLS backends this config does not select) plus 8 under `temp_detect/authority/` and `mb_ipc/authority/`. Keeping them is what allows diffing the import against upstream.
63: 
64: The 8 `authority/` dead files are NOT one kind:
65: 
66: - 6 under `temp_detect/authority/components/temp_detect/` (`temp_detect.c`, `volt_detect.c`, `bk_sensor.c` + 3 `.inc`) are SUPERSEDED by our own `temp_detect/bk7258_temp_detect.c`. Symbol sets are disjoint (authority `tempd_*`/`temp_sensor_*` vs ours `temp_detect_init`/`bk_sensor_*`/`volt_detect_*`), and our file's `<temp_detect.h>`/`<temp_detect_pub.h>` resolve into `wifi/glue/include/`, bypassing the directory entirely. Chain is `temp_detect.c` → `part2.inc` → `part3.inc`, `volt_detect.c` → `volt_detect_part2.inc`, so they only delete as a set.
67: - 2 under `mb_ipc/authority/` (`saradc_server.c`, `bk_phy_server.c`) are the CPU2-side servers. Their entry points ARE called from compiled code (`adc_driver.c:301-308`, `bk_sensor.c:95-102`) but behind `#if (CONFIG_CPU_CNT > 1)`, and `CONFIG_CPU_CNT` is undefined in both `build/{cp,ap}/.config` (`sys_config.h:93` says this port does not define it or advertise CPU2). They belong to the same thread as the AP SMP deadlock and `874125b`; a teammate re-enabling dual core will need them.
68: 
69: Naming is INCONSISTENT across the tree and the user noticed: team adaptation layers are `nuttx_port/` in `saradc`/`gpio`/`pm`/`aon_pmu`/`aon_rtc` but `glue/` in `wifi`; authority code is `authority/` everywhere except `wifi`, which uses `third_party/` — the one name `AGENTS.md:24` forbids. `mb_ipc` additionally carries both `authority/` and `authority_ap/` plus `authority_{cp,ap}_*.c` filename prefixes. `wifi` was built first and later modules changed convention without it following. Renaming is a separate PR: 146 files, two build systems, every `-I`, every wrapper's relative include, and `bk_prelude.h`'s own self-description.

1: ---
2: name: bk7258-worktree-build
3: description: "可复现地编译、打包、独立解码并全自动烧录 BK7258 worktree。Use when working in a BK7258 feature worktree, running the CP/AP build-to-flash flow, packaging all-app.bin, debugging build.sh paths, or needing the automatic reboot-bootloader flash (manual-reset fallback prompts during GetBus). Do not use for generic OpenVela boards or raw app.bin flashing."
4: ---
5: 
6: # BK7258 Worktree Build
7: 
8: ## Complete workflow
9: 
10: Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
11: build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:
12: 
13: ```bash
14: <skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
15:   --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
16:   --worktree <feature-worktree> \
17:   --jobs 12
18: ```
19: 
20: The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
21: `cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
22: are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
23: safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
24: the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
25: If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
26: is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
27: build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.
28: 
29: To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:
30: 
31: ```bash
32: <skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
33:   --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
34:   --worktree <feature-worktree> \
35:   --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
36: ```
37: 
38: To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
39: workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:
40: 
41: ```bash
42: <skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
43:   --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
44:   --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
45:   --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
46: ```
47: 
48: Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
49: image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
50: but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
51: `--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
52: worktree.
53: 
54: Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
55: streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
56: the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
57: as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
58: console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
59: (`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
60: `ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
61: vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
62: the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
63: that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
64: `Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
65: reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
66: hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
67: prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
68: stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
69: and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.
70: 
71: The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
72: worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
73: Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
74: runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
75: run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
76: platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
77: wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
78: SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
79: must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
80: immediately before launching it.
81: 
82: When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
83: commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
84: injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
85: appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
86: interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
87: through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
88: until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.
89: 
90: The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
91: produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
92: all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.
93: 
94: ## Scope
95: 
96: This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
97: linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
98: directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
99: checkout and not the worktree directory itself.
100: 
101: Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
102: `build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
103: `build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
104: `vendor/beken/boards/...`.
105: 
106: ## 1. Establish the worktree mapping
107: 
108: For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
109: the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:
110: 
111: ```bash
112: <skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
113:   --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
114:   --worktree <feature-worktree> \
115:   --component cp \
116:   --jobs 12
117: ```
118: 
119: Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
120: isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.
121: 
122: From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:
123: 
124: ```bash
125: readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
126: readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
127: ```
128: 
129: For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:
130: 
131: ```text
132: <worktree>/chips/bk7258
133: <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
134: ```
135: 
136: If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
137: building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
138: processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
139: restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
140: symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.
141: 
142: The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
143: tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
144: from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
145: `nuttx/` markers.
146: 
147: ## 2. Configure and build CP/AP
148: 
149: Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:
150: 
151: ```bash
152: ./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
153: ./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
154: ```
155: 
156: For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
157: minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
158: the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.
159: 
160: `build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
161: random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:
162: 
163: ```text
164: cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
165: cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
166: cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
167: cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
168: cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
169: ```
170: 
171: The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
172: Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
173: is not equivalent evidence.
174: 
175: ## 3. Package and independently decode
176: 
177: The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
178: The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
179: with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
180: runtime.
181: 
182: For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
183: preferred path:
184: 
185: ```bash
186: <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
187: ```
188: 
189: It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
190: independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
191: is considered valid.
192: 
193: The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
194: new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
195: `decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
196: Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
197: hardware evidence.
198: 
199: The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
200: and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
201: or `app1.bin` directly.
202: 
203: ## 4. Offline regression checks
204: 
205: Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:
206: 
207: ```bash
208: python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
209: ```
210: 
211: The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
212: The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
213: to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
214: be stable across invocation directories.
215: 
216: For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
217: then run the profile/package test described in
218: `board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
219: copy credentials into the repository.
220: 
221: ## 5. Troubleshooting
222: 
223: | Symptom | Cause | Action |
224: |---|---|---|
225: | `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
226: | Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
227: | Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
228: | Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
229: | `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
230: | CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
231: | Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
232: | Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
233: | `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
234: | No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
235: | `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
236: | Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
237: | Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |
238: 
239: ## Acceptance boundary
240: 
241: A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
242: passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
243: register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
244: target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

235: static int bk7258_ap_panic_notify(struct notifier_block *block,
236:                                   unsigned long action, void *data)
237: {
238:   FAR struct panic_notifier_s *info = data;
239:   uint32_t fault;
240: 
241:   (void)block;
242: 
243:   /* PANIC_TASK can describe a task-local assertion. Only kernel panic stages
244:    * are fatal evidence for this AP instance. */
245: 
246:   if (action != PANIC_TASK)
247:     {
248:       /* Encode the assertion location into the fault word so the CP-side
249:        * monitor can point at the failing source: high byte = a short hash of
250:        * the filename, low byte = line number. */
251: 
252:       if (info != NULL && info->filename != NULL)
253:         {
254:           uint32_t hash = 0;
255:           FAR const char *p;
256: 
257:           for (p = info->filename; *p != '\0'; p++)
258:             {
259:               hash = (hash << 1) ^ (hash >> 31) ^ (uint32_t)*p;
260:             }
261: 
262:           fault = BK7258_AP_FAULT_PANIC_BASE |
263:                   ((hash & UINT32_C(0xff)) << 8) |
264:                   ((uint32_t)(info->linenum & UINT32_C(0xff)));
265:         }
266:       else
267:         {
268:           fault = BK7258_AP_FAULT_PANIC_BASE |
269:                   ((uint32_t)action & UINT32_C(0xff));
270:         }
271: 
272:       bk7258_ap_record_fault(fault);
273:     }
274: 
275:   return 0;
276: }

看完了 `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 全貌(1916-2329)和 board 的 `bk7258_bringup.c`/`bk7258_boardinit.c`。你的方向对,但有一个**必须先看清、否则会踩坑的约束**:这段 init 不能直接内联进 `board_late_initialize()` 或 `board_app_initialize()`,必须保持"跑在专用大栈 kthread 上"。

## 现在 init 到底做了什么(已核实)

`bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 是一条很长的分层序列,分三段:

1. **通用**(非 runtime 也要):`bk7258_wifi_osal_init()` → `hw_init()` → `board_init()` → `lower_init()` → `lower_register()`(注册 `wlan0`)。
2. **vendor runtime 大段**(`#if CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME`):TRNG → bandgap → `srand(bk_rand())` → SARADC → sensor → event → LPO → AON RTC → `bk_phy/rf_adapter_init` → `vnd_cal_overlay` → `bk_wifi_init()`(起 vendor 的 core/kmsg/wpas 线程 + MAC 校准)。
3. 尾部 CPU 频率投票 120M→60M。

## 三个约束(决定怎么加进 board 流程)

1. **大栈**:app 现在用 `kthread_create("bk7258-wifi", 85, 8192, worker)` 跑它,注释明说"vendor init chain nests deeply,NSH 只给 4 KiB"。`board_late_initialize` 跑在 IDLE/bringup 任务上,栈不够,不能内联。→ 从 board 流程里**再起一个 8 KiB kthread** 去调 `bk7258_wifi_initialize()`,不是直接调用。

2. **PRNG 种子必须在"将要 pthread_create vendor 线程的那个 task group"里**(lower.c:2067-2074):NuttX 的 `srand` 种子存在 `task_info_s`,按 task group 隔离;`bk7258_wifi_osal_thread_create` 用 `pthread_create`,vendor 线程会 join 调用者的 group。所以 `srand` 和 `bk_wifi_init()` 必须在**同一个 kthread** 里跑,顺序不能拆。现在这条链在 `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 内部已经正确,搬进 board 流程时**别把它拆开**,整体搬走就行。

3. **幂等**:`bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 开头有 `if (g_bk7258_wifi.registered) return OK;`(line 1922),所以 boot 自动 init 之后,app 的 `ensure_ready()` 会变成秒退 no-op,不会重复跑。旧命令留着无害。

## 建议的落点

`board_late_initialize()` 里、`CONFIG_BK7258_COMPONENT_CP` 分支下,仿照 AP 那边 `kthread_create("bk7258-amp-init", ...)` 的既有模式,加一个 CP 侧 kthread:

```c
#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME
  kthread_create("bk7258-wifi", 85, 8192, bk7258_wifi_boot_init, NULL);
#endif
```

`bk7258_wifi_boot_init` 只做一件事:调 `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 然后 return(现成 `bk7258_wifi_runtime_worker` 的 body 就是它)。

## 要提醒你的一个决定

现在的 Kconfig 注释是**刻意**写成"Wi-Fi never starts at boot"(`bk7258_wifi_runtime` 是唯一 caller)。把它搬进 board 流程 = 反转这个决定:每次开机都跑完整 PHY 校准 + 起三个 vendor 线程,即使不用 wifi。不过 authority 板(`app_wifi_init`)本来就是 boot 时跑的,所以这反而**更对齐 authority**,不是偏离。

看完了三个参考板 + NuttX 标准驱动,结论清楚:**别的 board 都是"驱动 init 在 board bringup 阶段做,控制面交给标准 wapi 命令",没有一个把"驱动 init"做成 app 的**。你的判断对,runtime app 的 `init` 职责搬进 board 后,app 就该退场了。

## 三个参考实现(已核实源码)

**1. r528 + realtek(最典型)**
`realtek_wlan_bringup()` 在 `r528_late_initialize()` 里**同步**调用(`vendor/allwinnertech/chips/r528/r528_boot.c:971`),内部做 SDIO init + `realtek_wl_initialize(0)` → `realtek_netdev_init()` → `netdev_lower_register(NET_LL_IEEE80211)`(`realtek_netdev.c:414`)。控制面走 `wifi_test`/`wifi_manager` app + 标准 `wapi`。

**2. esp32s3**
`esp32s3_bringup()` 里 `board_wlan_init()` 同步调用(`esp32s3_bringup.c:235`),同样是 board_late_initialize 路径。

**3. NuttX 标准 `wifi_sim.c`(你要对齐的原生形态)**
`wifi_sim_init()` 只做两件事:`lower.iw_ops = &g_iw_ops` + 分配 priv(`wifi_sim.c:1979`)。它**完整实现了 `wireless_ops_s` 全部 14 个 handler**(connect/disconnect/essid/passwd/mode/auth/freq/bitrate/txpower/country/sensitivity/scan/range,`wifi_sim.c:335-351`),注册由调用者(driver probe)做。控制面就是 `apps/wireless/wapi`。

## 结论:runtime app 的职责要拆成两层

现在 `bk7258_wifi_runtime` 把两件事混在一个 app 里:

| 职责 | 该去的地方 | runtime app 现在的角色 |
|---|---|---|
| **驱动 init**(注册 `wlan0`,跑 vendor init chain) | `board_late_initialize`(别的 board 都这么做) | `init` 子命令 → 应删除 |
| **控制面**(scan/connect/txtest) | 标准 `wapi` 命令 | `scan`/`connect`/`txtest` → 被 wapi 取代 |

所以走 board init 后:**runtime app 整个可以删掉**,`ensure_ready()` 那套"裸命令自动先 init"的逻辑也随之消失——因为 `wlan0` 开机就在,wapi 直接能控制。

## 一个 bk7258 特有的差异点(不能照抄 realtek)

realtek/esp32s3 是**同步**在 `board_late_initialize` 里调 init,不需要 kthread。但 bk7258 的 vendor init chain 特别深(现有注释明确:NSH 栈 4KB 不够,要 8KB 大栈),所以 bk7258 得保留"**board_late_initialize 里起一个 8KB kthread**"这一步。这是 bk7258 独有的约束,不是通用模式——不影响"init 归 board、控制归 wapi"的大方向。

# Skill: ponytail

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | Build what's asked, but name the lazier alternative in one line. User picks. |
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |
| **ultra** | YAGNI extremist. Deletion before addition. Ship the one-liner and challenge the rest of the requirement in the same breath. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- lite: "Done, cache added. FYI: `functools.lru_cache` covers this in one line if you'd rather not own a cache class."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."
- ultra: "No cache until a profiler says so. When it does: `@lru_cache`. A hand-rolled TTL cache class is a bug farm with a hit rate."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

当前没有改代码，worktree 仍然是 clean。你说得对，这部分不能直接改，应该先把生命周期、WAPI 语义和启动时序设计清楚。

建议方案是“先迁移初始化职责，再迁移控制面，最后删除 runtime app”，分三阶段。

## 目标架构

```text
开机
  │
  ├─ board_late_initialize()
  │    └─ 创建 8 KiB Wi-Fi init kthread
  │          └─ bk7258_wifi_initialize()
  │                ├─ 硬件/时钟/OSAL
  │                ├─ PHY/RF/校准
  │                ├─ bk_wifi_init()
  │                └─ 注册 wlan0 + wireless_ops_s
  │
  └─ NSH / 用户态
       └─ wapi
            └─ NuttX wireless ioctl
                 └─ wireless_ops_s
                      └─ bk_wifi_* vendor API
```

`bk7258_wifi_runtime` 在迁移期间只作为对照工具，不再拥有 Wi-Fi 生命周期。

## 第一阶段：先把 boot init 迁出 runtime

当前 runtime app 同时承担两件事：

- `init`：启动 vendor Wi-Fi、注册 `wlan0`
- `scan/connect/txtest`：控制和诊断

第一阶段只迁移前者。

### 1. board 启动 Wi-Fi

在 `board/bk7258-devkit/src/bk7258_bringup.c` 里增加 board-owned 的一次性 kthread：

```text
board_late_initialize()
  └─ kthread_create("bk7258-wifi-init", ..., 8192, ...)
```

这个线程只调用现有的：

```c
bk7258_wifi_initialize();
```

不能直接在 `board_late_initialize()` 当前线程里调用，因为现有 runtime 已经明确验证过 vendor init 链需要大栈。

### 2. 保持初始化链完整

不拆动 `bk7258_wifi_initialize()` 内部的顺序，尤其保留：

```text
CPU 120 MHz vote
→ OSAL
→ HW init
→ board init
→ TRNG
→ bandgap
→ srand(bk_rand())
→ SARADC
→ sensor
→ event
→ LPO
→ AON RTC
→ PHY/RF adapter
→ calibration overlay
→ bk_wifi_init()
→ lower-half init
→ wlan0 register
→ CPU 60 MHz vote
```

这里 `srand()` 的位置不能挪。当前 vendor 线程通过 `pthread_create()` 从初始化线程的 task group 继承随机数状态。不能把前半段和 `bk_wifi_init()` 拆到不同线程。

### 3. 增加明确的启动状态

现在只有：

```c
bk7258_wifi_is_ready()
```

还不够表达失败原因。建议增加内部状态：

```text
NOT_STARTED
INITIALIZING
READY
FAILED
```

WAPI handler 根据状态返回：

- `NOT_STARTED` / `INITIALIZING`：`-EAGAIN` 或 `-ENODEV`
- `FAILED`：保存初始化错误并返回 `-EIO`
- `READY`：进入正常 vendor API

不能让用户看到 `wlan0` 但 Wi-Fi 还没初始化完，也不能静默把 WAPI 请求丢掉。

这里有两个启动时序选择：

### 方案 A：board 启动线程，NSH 不等待

优点：

- 不阻塞系统启动
- 保持现有异步结构
- 适合 vendor 初始化可能偶发变慢的情况

缺点：

- 用户刚进入 NSH 时，Wi-Fi 可能仍在初始化
- WAPI 第一次调用可能返回 `-EAGAIN`

### 方案 B：board 启动线程，`board_app_initialize()` 有界等待

优点：

- NSH 出现时，`wlan0` 基本已经可用
- 用户体验更接近普通 Vela board

缺点：

- 启动最长会被 Wi-Fi 初始化阻塞
- vendor 初始化失败会影响进入用户态的时延
- 如果 wait 逻辑写错，可能把启动卡死

我的建议是先采用 **方案 A**，但把初始化状态和日志做好。硬件验证稳定后，再决定是否在 `board_app_initialize()` 做一个短时间、有明确超时的等待。

## 第二阶段：把 WAPI 控制面补完整

WAPI 的关键调用顺序需要按 NuttX upper-half 的实际语义接起来。

当前 upper-half 已经规定：

```text
SIOCSIWENCODEEXT
  → wireless_ops_s.passwd()

SIOCSIWESSID + IW_ESSID_ON
  → wireless_ops_s.essid()
  → wireless_ops_s.connect()

SIOCSIWESSID + IW_ESSID_DELAY_ON
  → wireless_ops_s.essid()
  → 不 connect，用于 directed scan

SIOCSIWESSID + IW_ESSID_OFF
  → wireless_ops_s.disconnect()
```

因此不是简单地把 `bk7258_wifi_sta_connect()` 塞进一个 handler，而是要设计一份 NuttX-owned 的连接配置状态。

建议在 `struct bk7258_wifi_s` 里维护：

```text
SSID
PSK
PSK 是否已设置
BSSID 是否已设置
mode
auth/security 类型
当前连接请求状态
```

### `essid`

分三种语义：

- `IW_ESSID_DELAY_ON`
  - 只保存 SSID
  - 不连接
  - 供 directed scan 使用
- `IW_ESSID_ON`
  - 保存 SSID
  - 触发 `connect`
- `IW_ESSID_OFF`
  - 触发 `disconnect`
  - 清理连接状态

不能让 `essid` 自己偷偷调用 connect，因为 upper-half 已经负责 `ON → connect()`。

### `passwd`

接收 `SIOCSIWENCODEEXT` 的密码配置：

- 支持 WPA2-PSK
- 支持开放网络
- 严格限制 SSID 和 PSK 长度
- 不打印 PSK
- 不把 PSK 写入文件、日志或编译期配置
- 连接完成或断开后按设计清理敏感缓存

目前已有的 `bk7258_wifi_sta_connect(ssid, psk)` 长度检查可以复用，但需要把参数来源从 runtime app 的 argv 改为 lower-half 保存的配置。

### `connect`

只做：

```text
检查 READY
检查 SSID
检查密码/认证模式
调用现有 bk7258_wifi_sta_connect()
返回“请求已受理”
```

不在 ioctl 调用里同步等待 4-way handshake。连接仍然是异步的，由已有的：

```text
EVENT_WIFI_STA_CONNECTED
EVENT_WIFI_STA_DISCONNECTED
```

驱动 carrier 状态。

### `disconnect`

这里要先确认 vendor 侧真正对应的停止 API。不能为了让 WAPI 返回成功而写一个空 handler。

如果 vendor 有：

```c
bk_wifi_sta_stop()
```

就通过一个最薄的 team-owned wrapper 调用它。

如果 vendor 没有对应 API，则必须继续查 authority 的断开路径，不能直接返回成功，也不能自行手写一个“看起来等价”的断电或状态清理。

### 其他 handler

第一版不要为了“接口看起来完整”而制造假成功：

- `mode`
  - 支持 `IW_MODE_INFRA`
  - 其他模式返回 `-EOPNOTSUPP`
- `auth`
  - 只接受实际支持的 WPA2-PSK/open 配置
  - 不支持的认证方式返回 `-EOPNOTSUPP`
- `bssid`
  - 如果 vendor 连接配置支持固定 BSSID，再实现
  - 否则先返回明确的不支持
- `country/freq/range`
  - 没有真实 vendor 语义之前，保留不支持
- `scan`
  - 复用现有已经硬件验证过的实现

## 第三阶段：启用并验证纯 WAPI

需要确认 CP 配置包含：

```text
CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI=y
CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_LINK=y
CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_VENDOR_RUNTIME=y
CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI=y
CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI_CMDTOOL=y
```

runtime app 暂时仍然保留，但它只用于对照：

```text
旧路径:
bk7258_wifi_runtime connect ...

新路径:
wapi ...
```

验证顺序建议固定为：

1. 开机后不执行 `bk7258_wifi_runtime init`
2. 确认 `wlan0` 已注册
3. 执行 WAPI 查询
4. 用 WAPI 扫描
5. 用 WAPI 设置 SSID、PSK 和模式
6. 用 WAPI 发起连接
7. 检查 `CTRL-EVENT-CONNECTED`
8. 执行 DHCP
9. ping 网关
10. 对比 runtime 旧路径的扫描、关联、DHCP、ping 结果

硬件验收必须证明的是：

```text
Wi-Fi 在没有手动运行 runtime init 的情况下，
仅通过 board 启动和 WAPI 控制即可完成：
scan → association → 4-way handshake → DHCP → ping
```

WAPI 硬件验证通过前，不删除：

- `bk7258_wifi_runtime`
- 现有 `connect`
- 现有 `scan`
- 现有 `txtest`

1. 先删除 runtime 的 `init` 和 `ensure_ready()`，保留 `txtest` 一段时间作为低层诊断工具。
